The sample is small, but it creates a clear early contrast in defensive stability.

The two teams' 2025-26 meetings were competitive, averaging 6.00 total goals, so the safer way to express the edge is the overtime/shootout-inclusive moneyline rather than a regulation handicap.

Chicago's early defensive leakage, New York's home advantage and the higher location-based scoring projection all point toward the Islanders, while OT/SO protection reduces the risk from another close head-to-head.

analysis: This is one of the strongest statistical Over profiles on the slate. Vancouver averaged 2.68 goals scored and 3.80 allowed away from home in 2025-26, while Carolina averaged 3.88 scored and 3.05 allowed at home. Combining those splits produces approximately 2.87 expected goals for Vancouver and 3.84 for Carolina, for a 6.71-goal projection.

The direct matchup pushes the expectation higher. Their two 2025-26 meetings produced seven and ten goals, an 8.50 average, and both cleared 5.5. The early 2026-27 goaltending numbers also increase the scoring risk: Vancouver's Kevin Lankinen entered with a 4.50 GAA and .858 save percentage, while Carolina's Brandon Bussi was at 3.00 and .859.
The historical location model is already above six goals, both recent head-to-heads cleared the line, and the current goaltending profile provides another independent argument for six or more.

Montreal's home scoring profile from 2025-26 gives the Canadiens a reasonable edge despite Nashville's ability to keep games competitive. Montreal averaged 3.29 goals per home game, while Nashville's road offense averaged 2.88. The same split model produced a total expectation near 6.27, showing that Montreal does not need a low-event game to justify the moneyline.

The 2025-26 head-to-head meetings were tighter, with Montreal winning games that produced five total goals on average. Nashville also brings quality goaltending through Juuse Saros, which is an important counterweight. Montreal, however, has the stronger offensive environment at Bell Centre, and the overtime/shootout-inclusive market protects the selection if the game remains tied after regulation.

Ivan Demidov is out for Montreal, so the pick is not based on an assumption of full offensive strength. The preference is instead for Montreal's home profile and the protection provided by including overtime and the shootout.

Ottawa's strongest argument is the direct matchup. The Senators won all three meetings with Philadelphia in 2025-26, with scores of 2-1, 3-2 and 2-1. That 3-0 head-to-head record is more useful for the moneyline than for a goals market, especially because the games averaged only 3.67 total goals.

The home/away profile also gives Ottawa the stronger scoring side. The Senators averaged 3.34 goals at home in 2025-26, while Philadelphia allowed 3.12 on the road. Philadelphia's early 2026-27 offense has struggled badly, entering this stretch at only 1.25 goals per game with 4.25 allowed.

Jake Sanderson remains out for Ottawa, which lowers confidence in the Senators' defensive ceiling. Even so, an overtime/shootout-inclusive moneyline fits the recent matchup better than asking Ottawa to win in regulation.

The location model lands just above the target. San Jose averaged 3.05 goals scored and 3.66 allowed away from home in 2025-26, while St. Louis averaged 2.80 scored and 3.00 allowed at home. Combining those figures gives an expected total around 6.26 goals.

The head-to-head evidence is less aggressive. Their three 2025-26 meetings produced five, three and nine goals, averaging 5.67, with only one clearing 5.5. That makes this a higher-variance Over than the slate's other scoring selections. San Jose's current defensive/goaltending profile nevertheless leaves room for a high total, while Macklin Celebrini's day-to-day lower-body status is an important negative for the Sharks' offensive side.

At 1.91, the market requires only about a 52.4% break-even rate. The location model is above six goals, but the mixed head-to-head profile keeps this selection below the strongest Overs in the package.

The longer-term location model is relatively conservative, projecting approximately 5.59 total goals from Colorado's 2025-26 road production and Calgary's home splits. The direct matchup was more favorable to scoring: the three 2025-26 meetings averaged 6.33 total goals, including a nine-goal game.

The early 2026-27 form creates the strongest upward adjustment. Colorado opened the season with 14 goals through its first two games, while Calgary began winless and was conceding at a very high rate. That combination makes the current offensive/defensive trajectory substantially more aggressive than the 2025-26 split baseline.

The selection therefore relies on convergence between Colorado's elite early scoring, Calgary's defensive vulnerability and a head-to-head average already above the 5.5 threshold. The historical split model is the main caution and keeps this below the very top Over selections.

The 2025-26 home/away model is comfortably above the market line. Toronto averaged 2.85 goals scored and 3.71 allowed away from home, while Vegas averaged 3.54 scored and 2.95 allowed at home. Those splits produce approximately 2.90 expected Toronto goals and 3.62 for Vegas, or 6.52 total.

The direct matchup is even more aggressive. The two 2025-26 meetings produced nine and eleven total goals, an average of 10.00, with both comfortably clearing 5.5. Early 2026-27 results have also shown offensive upside from both sides, including a nine-goal Toronto game and a six-goal Vegas performance in their recent schedules.

The 6.52 split projection already supports the Over independently of the head-to-head. The direct meetings then provide a second, much stronger scoring signal, making six goals a realistic threshold despite the relatively short price.
Nationwide Arena in Columbus, Ohio hosts this game, with puck drop set for 7:00 p.m. ET on Friday, October 9.

Pittsburgh arrive after an explosive opening to the season. The Penguins scored seven against Philadelphia and six against Montreal, though the Montreal game also exposed a defensive weakness in a 6-5 overtime victory. A 3-2 loss to Winnipeg offered a more restrained picture before Washington put five past them in a 5-3 result. The swings matter more here than a simple record: Pittsburgh can create a large number of goals without always keeping the opposition quiet.

Columbus have been just as unpredictable. A 6-3 victory over Buffalo was followed by a 4-1 defeat to Utah, leaving them with seven goals scored and seven conceded through two games. The Blue Jackets' defensive depth is a further concern, with Ivan Provorov, Damon Severson and Dante Fabbro listed as unavailable in pre-game injury reports. Pittsburgh are missing Bryan Rust, so their attacking output cannot be assumed to continue at the same pace.

The longer-term home and away splits also point toward an open game. Pittsburgh averaged approximately 3.46 goals scored per away game last regular season, while Columbus averaged about 3.24 scored and 3.02 conceded at home. Those figures are no guarantee of six goals, but they explain why the line can be cleared with contributions from both attacks. Columbus' young forwards can punish Pittsburgh's lapses, while the Penguins have already shown they can score in bursts.
Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C. hosts this game, with puck drop set for 7:00 p.m. ET on Friday, October 9.

Washington host the Rangers with an offensive reference point already in place: the Capitals scored five in their recent victory over Pittsburgh. Their home attack was productive throughout the previous regular season, averaging roughly 3.39 goals per game, but the more interesting detail is that Washington also conceded only around 2.56 at home. That defensive record makes a high total less automatic than the scoring figures alone suggest.

The Rangers supply the counterweight. New York averaged approximately 3.20 goals per away game last season and conceded about 3.07, a road profile in which games can open up without the Rangers losing control of the score. That attacking capability is the main reason to lean toward goals rather than assume Washington's defense will dictate the evening.

A simple blend of last season's venue-specific scoring and conceding averages produces a total near 6.1 goals. That is a descriptive estimate rather than an expected-goals model, and it does not account for line combinations or goaltender confirmation. The most credible route past 5.5 is a competitive game in which both clubs contribute, rather than one side scoring four or five. Washington's recent scoring gives the total a solid starting point, and New York's established road production needs to supply the rest.
Canada Life Centre in Winnipeg, Manitoba hosts this game, with puck drop set for 8:00 p.m. ET on Friday, October 9.

Winnipeg face Anaheim in a matchup that puts the Ducks' road defending under scrutiny. Anaheim conceded approximately 3.54 goals per away game last season, the weakest venue-specific defensive figure among the eight clubs on this slate. Winnipeg's own home scoring average was around 3.02, so the Jets do not need an exceptional attacking night to put real pressure on the visitors. A recent 3-2 win over Pittsburgh also showed that Winnipeg can win without turning every game into a shootout.

The case for Winnipeg is not one-sided. The Jets conceded approximately 3.05 goals per home game last season, and Anaheim averaged just over three goals scored on the road, which leaves a real chance the Ducks can keep pace if Winnipeg's defensive structure is loose. The Jets' ability to manage the middle of the ice and deny Anaheim easy transition chances may prove more decisive than raw shot volume.

Goaltending is another variable. Winnipeg's starter should be checked close to puck drop, given the early-season workload and uncertainty around availability. Anaheim also play Calgary the following night, which could affect how they distribute minutes, although that is no proof of a weaker performance in Winnipeg. The home setting and Anaheim's road defensive problems are the main reasons to favor the Jets, while the relatively close price reflects a contest with meaningful risk.

analysis: Boston come into this matchup with momentum after a 6–1 win over Utah in which David Pastrnak produced two goals and two assists. That performance fits a broader offensive edge: the Bruins averaged 3.27 goals per game last season, compared with Philadelphia's 2.93. At home, Boston should be better placed to control possession, create sustained pressure and force a Flyers team with a difficult start to spend long stretches defending.

The main caution is Boston's own defensive record, as the Bruins conceded 3.01 goals per game in 2025/26. Philadelphia therefore still has a route into the game if Boston becomes loose without the puck.

Even so, the stronger scoring profile, home ice at TD Garden and recent attacking form give the Bruins the clearer path to the result. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

analysis: Vancouver's defensive numbers make this a favorable home spot for New Jersey. The Canucks conceded 3.83 goals per game last season and have already allowed 25 through their opening five games, with a 7–2 loss to Carolina again exposing problems in coverage and defensive-zone control.

New Jersey were not an elite scoring team last season at 2.76 goals per game, but this matchup offers a clearer opportunity to generate quality chances than the raw season average might suggest. The Devils still carry some risk because their own form has been inconsistent, so this is not simply a case of opposing Vancouver's defense.

The preference at Prudential Center comes from the combination of home ice and the Canucks' repeated difficulty preventing high-danger situations. If New Jersey can play with territorial control, they should have the better chance to turn those defensive issues into goals. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

analysis: Edmonton's opening four games have produced 22 goals for and 16 against, a combined average of 9.5 goals. The sample is still small, but it matches the type of game the Oilers can create: they averaged 3.44 goals scored and 3.23 conceded last season, while San Jose allowed 3.54 per game. With Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl driving the attack, Edmonton always carries enough top-end scoring to push a total upward quickly.
The Over is also helped by Edmonton's defensive vulnerability, which gives San Jose a realistic route to contribute rather than leaving the Oilers to carry the total alone.

The largest swing factors at SAP Center are Macklin Celebrini's availability and the confirmed goaltending matchup, but the statistical profile points toward a game with enough chances at both ends to clear five goals.

Minnesota's defensive profile provides the strongest foundation for a lower-scoring game. The Wild allowed only 2.87 goals per game last season and their recent 3–2 loss to Tampa Bay showed how their structure can keep a matchup controlled even against a talented opponent.

Florida conceded 3.34 per game, but Aleksander Barkov's absence removes an important piece of both the Panthers' attack and their two-way control through the middle. Florida still has enough skill to create pressure at home in Sunrise, while uncertainty in Minnesota's crease prevents this from being a low-risk Under.

Even so, a 6.5 line leaves some margin for a competitive game without requiring both teams to be completely shut down. If Minnesota can maintain its usual defensive discipline, the matchup is more likely to stay below seven goals than turn into an open exchange.

Buffalo bring the stronger attacking profile into this matchup after averaging 3.45 goals per game in 2025/26, compared with Utah's 3.27. Defensively, the teams were much closer, both conceding around 2.93 per game, which makes Buffalo's offensive depth and home-ice advantage more meaningful.

The Sabres were shut out 4–0 by Dallas, but that result came against elite goaltending and does not erase the broader scoring level they showed over the season. Utah arrive with their own warning sign after a 6–1 loss to Boston, a game that exposed how quickly the structure can unravel when pressure builds.

The starting-goaltender matchup at KeyBank Center can still move the balance, but Buffalo have the better combination of scoring depth, home environment and matchup leverage to respond from their previous defeat. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

analysis: Carolina hold a clear statistical edge on both sides of the puck. The Hurricanes averaged 3.55 goals scored and 2.88 conceded last season, while Chicago managed only 2.56 goals per game and allowed 3.29. That gap matters because Carolina's forecheck and puck pressure can force weaker teams to defend for long stretches, while the Blackhawks' limited scoring leaves less margin for error if they fall behind.
The Hurricanes reinforced that profile with a 7–2 win over Vancouver, highlighted by a Logan Stankoven hat trick.

Chicago's difficult start does not make the result automatic, but the matchup at United Center favors Carolina's depth, ability to recover pucks and stronger defensive structure. Across a full game, those advantages give the visitors the more reliable route to victory. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

Toronto can match almost any opponent for skill, but the Maple Leafs conceded 3.60 goals per game last season and have allowed 15 across their first five games of the new campaign. That defensive gap becomes more important in Denver, where Colorado can use home ice to dictate tempo and force Toronto into extended defensive sequences.

The Maple Leafs remain dangerous enough to punish mistakes, so this is not a one-sided matchup, but Colorado's balance is stronger. The Avalanche have more ways to win the game at Ball Arena, whether through sustained offense or by controlling the quality of chances against. Those numbers favor Ottawa at both ends, and home ice at Canadian Tire Centre gives the Senators another small edge in a matchup where territorial control could matter.

Nashville are still capable of punishing loose defensive play, as shown by their recent 5–2 win over Montreal, and Juuse Saros can keep the Predators competitive even when they are outshot. Ottawa's own availability on the blue line also adds some risk.

Even with those concerns, the Senators have the more balanced statistical profile and a stronger path to generating sustained offense at home. The moneyline selection includes overtime and a shootout, so a tie after regulation does not end the wager.

analysis: The defensive baseline points toward a controlled game. Tampa Bay conceded 2.79 goals per game last season and the Islanders allowed 2.88, while New York's offense averaged only 2.79. That combination makes it harder to project the Islanders carrying a high total unless the game becomes unusually open.

Ilya Sorokin's recent home performances at UBS Arena provide another layer of protection for the Under, and Tampa Bay's 3–2 win over Minnesota showed that the Lightning can manage a close contest without turning every game into a shootout.

Tampa's offensive talent is the obvious danger because a strong Lightning night can move the total quickly. Even so, the 6.5 line offers useful protection if the Islanders' lower-scoring profile and the defensive numbers hold.

Calgary's early defensive numbers are difficult to ignore. The Flames have allowed 23 goals in four games, an average of 5.75, including seven against Colorado. The sample is volatile, but it highlights the type of defensive breakdowns Anaheim can attack.

The Ducks averaged 3.23 goals scored and 3.51 conceded last season, a profile that naturally produced more open games at both ends. The main question is how much Calgary contributes: the Flames managed only 2.54 goals per game in 2025/26, so Anaheim may need to do a significant share of the scoring if that offensive level carries over.
Still, Calgary's current defensive instability at the Scotiabank Saddledome and Anaheim's own tendency to allow chances create enough routes to six goals for the Over to remain attractive.

Dallas enters this matchup showing clear offensive improvement. The Cowboys are coming off a 34-30 win over Houston after overcoming a double-digit halftime deficit, an important sign of progress in both Dak Prescott's execution and the offense's ability to produce under pressure. Dallas has been scoring around 30 points per game, with CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Javonte Williams giving the offense several ways to attack.

Tampa Bay enters with considerably more uncertainty, particularly around the quarterback position and an injury list that has affected important contributors. That makes sustaining drives against Dallas more difficult and increases the possibility of the Cowboys controlling field position and possession.

The -3.5 line does not require a dominant four-quarter performance. Dallas' improving offense, home advantage and Tampa Bay's personnel concerns provide enough statistical support for a victory by at least four points.

Jacksonville's improvement is visible beyond its win-loss record. The Jaguars have produced around 26 points per game and have been more efficient than Philadelphia at creating extra possessions. Their defense has generated 10 sacks and six interceptions, while their turnover differential reached +6, one of the strongest marks in the league.

Trevor Lawrence has also started efficiently, producing eight touchdown passes against only two interceptions while completing close to 70% of his attempts. That balance between quarterback efficiency and a defense creating turnovers is one of the strongest arguments for Jacksonville.

Philadelphia remains dangerous with Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley, but the Eagles have been less consistent offensively and have not generated the same defensive pressure. Jacksonville's current trajectory supports asking the Jaguars to win by more than a field goal.

Cincinnati has lost some momentum after a positive opening, but its offensive ceiling remains higher than Miami's current level. The recent defeats should not automatically be interpreted as a collapse: the Bengals still have the structure and playmakers required to create separation against vulnerable defenses.

Miami has shown flashes of improvement, but consistency remains a problem. The Dolphins have struggled to sustain production across four quarters and have repeatedly allowed negative sequences to turn competitive games against them.

The -3.5 line gives Cincinnati a manageable target. The Bengals need only a four-point victory, and their superior offensive ceiling provides a reasonable path to covering if they return closer to the execution shown earlier in the season.

Minnesota's strong start is supported by defensive indicators rather than results alone. The Vikings have generated 16 sacks and have operated with a turnover differential around +5, repeatedly creating extra possessions for their offense.

New Orleans has shown signs of offensive improvement and should not be treated as an easy opponent. The major difference is ball security and defensive pressure. Minnesota has consistently turned pressure into negative plays and turnovers, while the Saints have struggled in that area.

That profile travels well because Minnesota does not need to dominate possession to change games. At 1.83, the price is attractive for a team combining strong results with sustainable defensive production.

The appeal of this market starts with the low total. Cleveland has generated significant defensive pressure, including double-digit sacks and several interceptions. Those defensive plays do not necessarily hurt an Over this low because turnovers and short fields can create scoring opportunities.

The Jets have also begun showing better offensive execution. Their passing game has protected the football reasonably well and has become more efficient at sustaining drives, while Cleveland has shown enough touchdown production to contribute its share.

With the threshold at only 37.5 points, this game does not need to become a shootout. A 21-17 result is already enough. Recent offensive improvement combined with the possibility of short-field scoring supports the Over.

Indianapolis is improving and enters after a convincing performance, so this matchup should not be evaluated simply by comparing records. The Colts have shown better offensive rhythm and are increasingly capable of sustaining drives.

Pittsburgh's advantage comes from matchup context and home field. At Acrisure Stadium, the Steelers can lean on defensive pressure and field position, two factors that become particularly important in evenly matched games. Pittsburgh does not need to cover a spread here; it only needs to find a way to win.
The Colts' progress makes this one of the more competitive selections in the group, but Pittsburgh's home environment and defensive ability provide enough support for the moneyline.

Houston's record does not fully reflect the team's potential, but the Texans now need to convert improved stretches of football into complete games. Their offense has enough talent to create separation, while the defense has the personnel to make life difficult for a Tennessee attack that has also struggled to turn possessions into points.

Tennessee has shown some improvement, but offensive consistency remains a major limitation. If Houston establishes an early advantage and forces the Titans into obvious passing situations, the matchup becomes considerably more favorable for the Texans.

The -6.5 line is demanding because Houston must win by at least seven, so this is not one of the safest selections. The argument is that Houston's underlying talent and improving execution can finally produce a result more convincing than its record suggests.

Washington's start has been uneven, but the Commanders have enough offensive talent to improve quickly if they reduce mistakes and finish drives more efficiently. Recent results make this a more difficult matchup than the moneyline price suggests, because New York has started the season better.

The reason to remain with Washington is the combination of home field and the expectation that its offensive efficiency can move closer to the level of its personnel. This is a matchup where the Commanders do not need to cover a handicap; any victory is sufficient.
New York's stronger early record makes this one of the higher-risk predictions in the group. Washington needs its recent signs of improvement to translate into four quarters of cleaner football.

Detroit combines strong recent performance with excellent underlying offensive numbers. The Lions have been producing close to 30 points per game and nearly 390 yards, while Jared Goff has opened the season with excellent touchdown-to-interception efficiency.

The matchup becomes even more favorable because Arizona has suffered a major offensive-line loss, with left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. unavailable for the remainder of the season. That is particularly damaging against a Detroit defense that has been among the league leaders in sacks.

Arizona has enough offensive talent to remain competitive, but Detroit currently has the stronger quarterback efficiency, pass rush and overall scoring profile. Because this is a moneyline rather than a handicap, the Lions only need to convert those advantages into a victory.

San Francisco has been one of the league's most productive teams, combining an unbeaten start with roughly 30 points and close to 390 yards per game. Brock Purdy has been exceptionally efficient, producing double-digit touchdown passes with very few interceptions, while Christian McCaffrey continues to give the offense balance.
Seattle is also playing good football and has created pressure and turnovers at a strong rate. That is precisely why taking +3.5 is more attractive than requiring San Francisco to win outright.

The 49ers can lose by a field goal and the selection still wins. With San Francisco's offensive efficiency and strong start providing the baseline, those extra points offer valuable protection in a difficult divisional road matchup.

Atlanta's chances increase considerably because Baltimore enters with uncertainty around Lamar Jackson, who has been dealing with an ankle injury. Baltimore with a fully healthy Jackson is a very different opponent, making his availability and mobility one of the most important variables in this matchup.

Atlanta has also shown genuine offensive progress. Bijan Robinson has been highly productive on the ground, giving the Falcons a way to control possession and keep Baltimore's offense on the sideline. That becomes even more valuable if the Ravens cannot generate their normal explosive-play volume.

This prediction is therefore closely connected to Baltimore's injury situation. If Jackson is unavailable or clearly limited, Atlanta's home-field advantage, running game and improving offensive execution make the 1.59 moneyline substantially more attractive.
